The corpus is generated over fixed axes, so it can only score a gap it has a
program for. `runs` can reach 100% with every site below still refusing.
`scripts/capability-probes/` holds a hand-written program per gap; run
`vl run scripts/capability-probes.vl` to grade the ones covered so far.

  BY WORDING — every literal in compiler/*.vl whose SENTENCE concedes the
  refused program was type-valid. A refusal is not obliged to concede, so this
  is a floor: 517 of the compiler's 533 emit-side refusal sites say nothing
  about legality and none of them can appear here.
  ZERO  compiler/a.vl:4                 'an \\"escaped\\" quote that is not yet implemented'
  ZERO  compiler/b.vl:2                 'closures over `T` not supported yet in this position'
  HIT   compiler/a.vl:2                 'emitProgram: `==` over f64[] has no lowering'
  ZERO  compiler/a.vl:5                 'padded and Not Yet Callable'
  ZERO  compiler/b.vl:3                 'ü a literal that is not supported by codegen and runs far pa'

  (a gap moved into typecheck.vl stops looking like a gap — the program
   compiles no better than before, so these count the same as emit-side ones)

  BY WITNESS — a refusal literal some check-clean program provably reaches.

  a witness that starts running comes OFF the list in the PR that closed it.
